This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows :
On 07-05-2024 at about 6.25 p.m., the petitioner was standing on the side of the 3 rd cross road, Vinayakanagar, JP Nagar 5th Phase, Bengaluru.

At that time, the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-LC-4461 ridden by its rider in rash and negligent manner, came at high speed from east to west direction, towards extreme left side of the road and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner has fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she took treatment as an in-patient.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Earlier to the accident, she was studying in 3rd standard, at Urdu Government School, JP Nagar,
Bengaluru and she was brilliant student.
Due to accidental injuries she is not able to attend the classes and also not able to participate in sports and cultural activities conducted in the school.

Now she is suffering from severe pain in her both legs,
cannot stand, cannot walk, she is totally bed ridden and she is not able to do her normal routine activities as she was doing prior to the accident.
The Jayanagar Traffic Police have registered the case against the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-LC-4461 for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel.
But, they did not choose to file their written statements.
4. In order to prove her case, the petitioner has got examined her mother/natural guardian as P.W.1 and got marked total 16 documents as Ex.P.1 to 16.
Further, she has got examined one more witness namely Dr. Chidanand K.J.C. as P.W.2 and closed her side.
On the other hand, the respondents have not adduced any evidence on their behalf.

5. The following points arise for my consideration:

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?

Bengaluru, the offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-LC-4461, ridden by its rider in rash and negligent manner, came at high speed from east to west direction, towards extreme left side of the road and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner has fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, she was studying in 3rd standard at Urdu Government School, JP Nagar, Bengaluru and she was brilliant student.
Due to accidental injuries she is not able to attend the classes in the school and also not able to participate in sports and cultural activities conducted in the school.

Now she is suffering from severe pain in her both legs, cannot stand, cannot walk, she is totally bed ridden and she is not able to do her normal routine activities as she was doing prior to the accident.
9. In order to prove her case, the petitioner has examined her mother/natural guardian as P.W.1.
The P.W.1 has filed her examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein she has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of her oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 16 documents as Ex.P.1 to 16.

On meticulously going through the above police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 8, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-LC-4461 and dashing the same to the petitioner, who was crossing the said road.
Further it reveals that, due to said impact the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries on both the legs.

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.8, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-LC-4461 and dashing the same to the petitioner, who was crossing the said road and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries to her both the legs.
11.

Further, the above oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle i.e. respondent No.1 & 2 respectively, as they did not choose to file their written statements and contest the case of the petitioner.

The P.W.1 has clearly deposed in her evidence that, on 07-05-2024 at about 6.25 p.m.,
when the daughter/petitioner was standing on the side of the 3rd cross road, Vinayakanagar, JP Nagar 5th Phase, Bengaluru, the offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-LC-4461, ridden by its rider in rash and negligent manner, came at high speed from east to west direction, towards extreme left side of the road and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner has fell down and sustained grievous injuries to her both the legs.

12. The Ex.P.4 spot mahazar and Ex.P.5 sketch also clearly speaks that, the accident has taken place on the extreme left side of 15 feet wide 3rd Cross road, Vinayakanagar, JP Nagar 5th Phase,
Bengaluru, due to dashing of offending motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-LC-4461 to the petitioner,
who was crossing the road.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.6, the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident was not due to any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there is no negligence on the part the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending vehicle.
There is absolutely no material on record to show that, there was any contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner in the cause of accident.

In such circumstances,
there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg.
No. KA-05-LC-4461, the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

13. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.7 wound certificate, Ex.P.11 discharge summary, Ex.P.13 OPD slip, Ex.P.14 case-sheet, Ex.P.15 MLC extract and Ex.P.16 x- ray, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and she has suffered right isolated tibia fracture and left leg both bone fracture.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

14. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

entities.text:
Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 15. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 16. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 07-05-2024 at about 6.25 p.m., on the extreme left side of 3rd Cross road, Vinayakanagar, JP Nagar 5th Phase, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-LC-4461.
Hence, I answer point No.1 in Affirmative.
17. Point No.2:

While answering above point this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has caused due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-LC-4461 and she has sustained grievous injuries.
As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, she has sustained right isolated tibia fracture and left leg both bone fracture and for the said injuries she has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

To prove her age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of her Aadhar card,
which is marked as Ex.P.9.
As per Ex.P.9, the date of birth of the petitioner is 15-11-2014.
The accident has taken place on 07-05-2024 at about 6.25 P.M.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 10 years.
In the case on hand, petitioner is admittedly a minor of the age of 10 years as on the date of accident and she has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life,
loss of prospects of marriage etc.
18.

In the present facts and circumstances of the case, it is relevant to refer the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, in the case of Master Karthik R. S/o V. Rajababu V/s National Insurance Co. Ltd., and another, reported in MFA No.426/2020 (MV-I) C/w MFA No.4124/2020 (MV-I) and MFA No.7008/2021 (MV-I), dated 27-09-2024.

In the said decision, at Para No.25, the Hon'ble High Court has clearly held that:

sentences.text: In light of the fact that, the Apex Court has accepted that, the minor would suffer a pecuniary loss and has awarded compensation under this account in the case in Kajal's case and Ayush's case and it has held that, the minor should be awarded non- pecuniary loss for the injuries suffered in Master Mallikarjun's case, the ideal method for determining the compensation for minor would be to combine both the components i.e. compensation for the pecuniary loss (as determined in Kajal's and Ayush's cases) and also for the non-pecuniary loss (as determined in Master Mallikarjun 's case).

This methodology in determining the compensation would essentially take care of both the pecuniary and non pecuniary loss that a child would suffer as a result of a disability and would therefore constitute 'just compensation' as contemplated under the M.V. Act."
19.

In the light of above decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, the petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
i) Loss on future income: The petitioner has averred that due to accidental injuries,
she has sustained grievous injuries and she has suffered disability.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor, who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered right isolated tibia fracture and left leg both bone fracture and for the said injuries the petitioner has undergone surgery i.e. CRIF with TENS nail for both legs.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability of 32% to the left lower limb, 25% to the right lower limb and 18% to the whole body.

The Ex.P.7 wound certificate,
Ex.P.11 discharge summary, Ex.P.13 OPD slip, Ex.P.14 case sheet, Ex.P.15 MLC extract and Ex.P.16 x-ray are clear evident that, the petitioner has suffered the above mentioned injuries and she has undergone surgery for the said injuries.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, there is no disability to him and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 07-05-2024 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 15-03-2025,
which is after lapse of 9 months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further he has stated that, the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before completion of full treatment.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

sentences.text:
If the disability had been assessed after future surgery,
perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.
Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, both the fractures are united and implants are in situ.
Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that,
considering the disability of 13% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified

. Hence, in the Afifa Taj vs Mala on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46133201/

The petitioner is the resident of Vinayakanagar, 3rd Cross, JP Nagar 5th Phase, Bengaluru, the accident has taken place on 3rd Cross road, Vinayakanagar, JP Nagar 5th Phase, Bengaluru and she has taken treatment at Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics, Bengaluru.

In all, petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.12,01,080/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.

21. Liability: The contention of the petitioner that, as on the date of accident the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-LC-4461 and the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.2 in respect of said vehicle was valid from 18-01-2021 to 17-01-2026, has remained undisputed in the case.
Further, there is no evidence on record to show that, there is any breach of terms and conditions of the said policy.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-LC-4461 the accident has occurred and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons,
holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.12,01,080/- from the respondent No.2, I answer Point No.2 in Partly Affirmative.

The petition is partly allowed with costs.
